title: The State and Fate of Multilingual, Contextual Evaluation in the NLP World
abstract: arXiv:2610.36990v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Multilingual evaluation benchmarks are the primary instrument for assessing whether large language models generalize beyond English, yet the adequacy of these benchmarks has received little systematic scrutiny. We present a data-driven audit of 51 recent multilingual benchmarks spanning 242 datasets and 219 languages, organized around three pillars: coverage, representativeness, and rigor. Our analysis reveals that coverage is wide but thin with 36% of evaluated languages appearing in only a single benchmark, entire regions (Oceania, the Americas, Central Asia) are near-zero, and a stark task equity gap leaves low-resource languages evaluated on only 1-3 task categories versus 14 for high-resource languages. translated_title: NLP世界中多语言情境化评估的现状与命运
translated_abstract: 多语言评估基准是评估大型语言模型能否泛化到英语之外的主要工具，然而这些基准的充分性却很少受到系统性审查。我们对51个近期多语言基准进行了数据驱动的审计，涵盖242个数据集和219种语言，围绕三大支柱展开：覆盖率、代表性和严谨性。我们的分析显示，覆盖率广而浅：36%的被评估语言仅出现在单一基准中，整个地区（大洋洲、美洲、中亚）的覆盖几乎为零，且存在显著的任务公平性差距——低资源语言仅在1-3个任务类别上得到评估，而高资源语言则有14个。代表性在结构上受到损害：从英语翻译仍是主要的构建策略，所有数据集-语言实例中有56%为翻译版本，这引入了伪影和以英语为中心的框架，而（原文在此处截断）……
tldr: 该论文对51个多语言NLP评估基准进行了数据驱动的系统性审计，揭示了多语言评估中覆盖率浅薄、地区严重缺失、低资源语言任务类别匮乏以及过度依赖英语翻译等结构性缺陷。
en_tdlr: This paper presents a data-driven audit of 51 multilingual NLP benchmarks across 242 datasets and 219 languages, revealing critical gaps in coverage, severe regional underrepresentation, task inequity for low-resource languages, and structural bias from English-centric translation.
